item.title: Extreme Localization via a Singular Edge Mode in an Asymmetric Linkage System
item.description: arXiv:2610.15041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanical localized modes generally retain exponentially decaying tails, whereas confinement to a single structural unit is difficult to achieve without resonators, flat-band lattices or topological design. To address this need, an asymmetric linkage system is introduced in which geometry tunes a boundary mode from finite localization to its extreme limit. Each cell comprises two unequal rigid bars connected by a torsional spring and is described by one generalized coordinate. Linearization and coordinate transformation yield a tridiagonal model and closed-form expressions for the edge mode frequency and spatial decay ratio. The analysis identifies the configurations supporting a singular edge mode at which its decay ratio vanishes, leaving only the boundary cell active in the linear regime. Simulations show near-complete localization under finite-amplitude excitation, and experiments reproduce the configuration-dependent transition from bulk transmission to boundary confinement. These results establish a minimal and analytically tunable platform for mechanical localization
item.dc:creator: Myeonggyun Joo, Dongwook Kwak, Rajesh Chaunsali, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Jinkyu Yang

item.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is neutrally stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Daniels, Simon Eskin, Tel Fahrendholz, Arnd Scheel

item.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll \phi_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > \phi_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle \phi \rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(\phi) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.
item.dc:creator: Yoritaka Iwata, Yasuhiro Takei

item.title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.16290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka D. Bhoyar, Prashant M. Gade

item.title: Feedback-Controlled Self-Trapping of Solitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.18191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chip-scale microresonator-based frequency combs, commonly referred to as microcombs, are promising sources for field-deployable metrology applications. However, intrinsic microresonator noise can make it difficult to generate microcombs with sufficiently low noise for applications. A widely used approach to overcome this limitation is to trap the DKS in the microresonator by phase-modulating the pump laser, although integrating a low-noise modulation reference in a fully on-chip platform remains challenging. Here, we propose an optoelectronic self-trapping scheme in which the impact of intrinsic microresonator noise on microcomb repetition-rate jitter is suppressed through feedback-controlled phase modulation of the driving laser so that the intrinsic noise of the laser sets the ultimate performance limit. This modification eliminates the need for an external low-phase-noise RF source, thereby enabling chip integration. We develop both analytical and numerical models for the proposed system and benchmark its performance against conventional externally referenced bulk implementations, showing that the proposed approach achieves comparable microcomb noise suppression while maintaining chip-scale compatibility.
item.dc:creator: Raonaqul Islam, Pradyoth Shandilya, Yunxiang Song, Alioune Niang, Gary Carter, Thomas Carruthers, Curtis Menyuk, Ergun Simsek

item.title: Diffusion Limited Aggregation in Ants Biting off Wall Paint
item.description: arXiv:2504.13400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusion limited aggregation (DLA) is a well studied phenomenon in which diffusing particles cumulatively aggregate on a starting fixed seed point, forming a pattern which is fractal in structure. Here we report an interesting DLA process arising from ants biting off wall paint. The structures arising from this long process are analyzed and found to have a fractional dimension between 1 and 2. The DLA formations observed in nature are mostly a result of various kinds of inanimate or micro-biological particles diffusing and aggregating. What makes the present observation interesting is that it involves live insects which may be guided by sight, smell etc. A simple theoretical model of the process is simulated, and the results agree well with the experimental observations.
item.dc:creator: Suvrajyoti Chatterjee, Saba Firoze, Tabish Qureshi

item.title: Experimental observation of ballistic correlations in integrable turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2601.21085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unequal-time correlation functions fundamentally characterize emergent statistical properties in complex systems, yet their direct measurement in experiments is challenging. We report the experimental observation of two-time, ballistic correlations in a photonic platform governed by the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. Using a recirculating optical fiber loop with heterodyne field detection, we acquire the full space-time dynamics of partially coherent optical waves and extract the intensity correlator in stationary states of integrable turbulence. The correlators collapse under ballistic rescaling and quantitatively agree with predictions from Generalized Hydrodynamics evaluated using the density of states obtained via inverse scattering analysis of the recorded fields. Our results provide a direct, parameter-free test of GHD in an integrable waves system.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Charnay et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 097202 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Elias Charnay, Adrien Escoubet, Francois Copie, Stephane Randoux, Thibault Bonnemain, Alvise Bastianello, Pierre Suret

item.title: Neuromorphic Computing Based on Parametrically-Driven Oscillators and Frequency Combs
item.description: arXiv:2604.21861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parametrically driven oscillators exhibit distinct dynamical regimes that strongly influence their computational capability as physical reservoirs. Here, we demonstrate reservoir computing in a two-mode system exhibiting 2:1 parametric resonance using Mackey--Glass, R\"ossler, and Lorenz chaotic time-series prediction tasks. Mapping the normalized mean squared error over parameter space reveals that the lowest prediction errors consistently occur within the parametric resonance regime, where nonlinear interactions are activated while temporal coherence is preserved. In contrast, although frequency-comb states increase spectral dimensionality, prediction performance degrades in the chaotic comb regime due to loss of phase coherence. We further show that the modulation depth $\Delta \text{F}$, detuning $\kappa$, damping ratio $\gamma_{21}$, and input data rate systematically reshape the accessible dynamical regimes and thereby control the reservoir performance. These results identify parametric resonance as a robust operating regime for oscillator-based neuromorphic computing and establish dynamical regime engineering as a route toward physical reservoir optimization.
item.dc:creator: Mahadev Sunil Kumar, Adarsh Ganesan

item.title: Real-time identification of the onset of financial rogue waves
item.description: arXiv:2606.31475v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extreme events in financial systems, often captured by indicators such as volatility, remain difficult to identify close to their onset. Volatility shares many statistical properties with other natural, complex systems which experience extreme events, which we explore in this manuscript. We extend the analogy between rogue waves in optical and hydrodynamical systems to financial volatility by identifying rogue-wave-like peaks with similar statistical properties. We use a Schr\"odinger equation where the potential follows the shape of a Kerr nonlinearity to examine the properties of financial volatility indices within a moving time window. We see evidence of Anderson localisation as a rogue peak approaches in the VIX, and show that the numerical gradient of the system's minimum eigenvalue reliably spikes at the onset of an extreme event. We adapt our methodology to simulate the real-time arrival of data, and show that all but one of the VIX's major peaks can be detected given a reasonable amount of history. We then perform two out-of-sample tests, one for the VXO index, and one for the VSTOXX index, and successfully replicate our initial results, identifying all but one major peak (87.5% or 7/8) in both cases. This method of analysis shows considerable promise as a tool for identifying potential financial crises, aiding in their mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Rosie Hayward, Orla Lennon, Fabio Biancalana
